messages.content:
Work out the ICD-10-AM principal diagnosis category for the episode below. The principal diagnosis is the single condition established after investigation to be chiefly responsible for the patient's episode of admitted care. It is not the patient's most serious comorbidity, not the presenting symptom, and not the procedure performed.

Think in three steps: first name the condition chiefly responsible for the admission, second name the ICD-10-AM chapter letter it belongs to, third give the three-character category.

Example 1
Hospital course: A 72-year-old man with a 50 pack-year smoking history was admitted with three days of worsening breathlessness and purulent sputum. Spirometry showed an FEV1/FVC ratio of 0.52. He was treated with nebulised bronchodilators, oral prednisolone and antibiotics for an infective exacerbation of his long-standing airflow limitation.
Answer: Irreversible airflow limitation in a heavy smoker with an infective exacerbation is chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, chapter J, category J44.
CODE: J44

Example 2
Hospital course: A 58-year-old man presented with crushing central chest pain radiating to the jaw. The electrocardiogram showed ST elevation in the anterior leads and high-sensitivity troponin rose from 40 to 2100 ng/L. He underwent primary percutaneous coronary intervention with a stent to the proximal left anterior descending artery.
Answer: ST elevation with a rising troponin and culprit-vessel stenting is an acute myocardial infarction, chapter I, category I21.
CODE: I21

Hospital course:
Discharge Summary:

Patient Name: [REDACTED]

Age: 70 years

Sex: Male

Medical History:

The patient was diagnosed with advanced renal cell carcinoma and was receiving Ipilimumab/Nivolumab therapy. He presented with new-onset fatigue and dizziness after two cycles of therapy.

Hospital Course:

During the hospital course, the patient underwent a physical examination, which revealed normal visual fields. Laboratory assessment showed mild hyponatremia, with low TSH and free T4. Morning ACTH and cortisol were also low. MRI brain showed pituitary enhancement.
Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]
Treatment:

Ipilimumab/Nivolumab therapy was temporarily stopped, and the patient was started on hydrocortisone 10mg/5mg in the morning and afternoon, respectively, as well as a weight-based dose of levothyroxine. The patient demonstrated clinical improvement and was restarted on PD-1 monotherapy.

Follow-up:

The patient was given "sick day" instructions for stress dosing of hydrocortisone and a medical alert bracelet. Key concepts of management involve high index of clinical suspicion, appropriate localization of endocrine dysfunction, hormone replacement, and close monitoring. Immune-related endocrine events are unique as the manifestations are often irreversible, and patients often require lifelong hormone replacement.

Hospital Disposition:

The patient was discharged from the hospital after clinical improvement. It is recommended that ICI is held for any-grade hypophysitis. Once patients demonstrate stability on hormonal replacement, ICI can be restarted. Higher-grade hypophysitis can be managed with an initial pulsed dose of corticosteroids. The patient was instructed to continue receiving follow-up medical care.

Write your reasoning in at most three short sentences, then a final line of exactly 'CODE: <letter><digit><digit>'.

text:
Immune checkpoint inhibitor (ipilimumab/nivolumab) hypophysitis with secondary adrenal insufficiency and central hypothyroidism is the condition chiefly responsible for this admission. That is drug-induced hypopituitarism, a disorder of the pituitary gland in chapter E. It falls under category E23.

CODE: E23
